stem: Which tool is widely used to send and inspect API requests manually?
options: Postman
Photoshop
Excel
Wireshark
explanation: Postman.

stem: What should a test check about the response of a successful GET request?
options: The status code, headers and body
Only the colour of the page
Only the time that the server started up
Only the size of the request that was sent
explanation: The status code, headers and body content or schema.

stem: Which API test is a good negative test?
options: Sending an invalid token and expecting 401
Sending a valid request and expecting 200
Repeating a valid request and expecting the same data
Sending a valid request after a long pause
explanation: Sending invalid input or missing authentication and expecting a proper 4xx error.

stem: How can Postman collections run automatically in a pipeline?
options: With the Newman command-line runner
By exporting them to a spreadsheet for the whole team
By emailing them to the developers
By sharing the screen during the meeting
explanation: With the Newman command-line runner.

stem: What does contract testing verify between a consumer and a provider service?
options: That messages match the agreed contract between them
That both services use the same programming language and framework
That both services run on the same server
That both services have the same number of tests as the work grows
explanation: That requests and responses match the agreed contract, so changes do not break the consumer.

stem: Why run automated tests in a CI pipeline?
options: To catch regressions early on every change for the business
To avoid writing some of the manual test cases
To make the application use less memory when it runs in most cases
To remove the need for code review
explanation: To catch regressions early on every change.

stem: Which of these is a common CI server?
options: Jenkins
Zeplin
Notion
Miro
explanation: Jenkins.

stem: What is a flaky test?
options: One that passes and fails without a code change from the start
One that usually fails on the first run
One that takes more than a second to run each time
One that has no assertions at all
explanation: A test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails without any code change.

stem: A suite of 2,000 UI tests takes two hours in CI. What is the best way to speed it up?
options: Run the tests in parallel on several workers
Run the tests just once a month
Remove the assertions from each test in the long run
Run the tests on a developer laptop
explanation: Run the tests in parallel across several machines or containers and keep only valuable UI tests.

stem: What does shift-left testing mean?
options: Testing earlier in the development lifecycle
Testing just after the product is released
Testing with just the left half of the team
Testing the left side of each page
explanation: Testing earlier in the development lifecycle, for example unit and integration tests in CI.

stem: Which tool is commonly used for load testing web applications?
options: Apache JMeter
Selenium IDE
Postman collections
Cucumber
explanation: Apache JMeter (also k6 and Locust).

stem: What is the goal of a load test?
options: Measure behaviour under the expected number of users
Find spelling mistakes on the pages for the project within the team
Check that the colours meet the style guide at that stage
Verify that the code compiles on each machine in the team
explanation: To measure behaviour under expected levels of concurrent users.

stem: The average response time is 300 ms but the 95th percentile is 4 seconds. What does this show?
options: A share of users gets a much slower experience
The system is much faster than the average suggests
The test ran for too short a time
The server is using too little memory
explanation: Some users have a much slower experience; percentiles reveal outliers that the average hides.

stem: What is the difference between a load test and a stress test?
options: Load uses expected traffic, stress goes past the limit
Load uses one user, stress uses two users as the work grows
Load checks the design, while stress checks the colours
They are two names for the same test in most teams during the project
explanation: A load test uses expected load; a stress test pushes beyond it to find the breaking point.

stem: Throughput stops growing as users increase while response time climbs. What is the likely situation?
options: A resource is saturated and has become the bottleneck
The test tool is generating too few requests at that stage
The network cable is faster than needed
The browser cache is working too well
explanation: A bottleneck: some resource (CPU, database connections, locks) is saturated.

stem: Which tool automates browser actions for testing web applications?
options: Selenium
Figma
Jira
Maven
explanation: Selenium (also Cypress and Playwright).

stem: What is a locator in UI test automation?
options: An expression that finds an element on the page
A file that stores the test results
A server that runs the browser somewhere in the cloud
A report that lists the failed tests
explanation: An expression such as an id, CSS selector or XPath that finds an element on the page.

stem: A test clicks a button before the page has loaded and fails at random. What is the right fix?
options: Wait explicitly for the element to be clickable
Add a fixed pause of thirty seconds at that stage
Run the test again until it passes in a real project
Remove the click from the test
explanation: Use explicit waits for the element or condition instead of fixed sleeps.

stem: What is the Page Object Model?
options: A pattern that wraps each page's elements and actions in a class
A report format for test results
A way to record the screen while tests run for the project in a real project
A database of test data for each page at that stage in most teams
explanation: A pattern that wraps each page's elements and actions in a class to reduce duplication.

stem: Which tests are best candidates for automation?
options: Stable, repetitive checks that run on every release during the project
One-off tests of a design that will change next week
Tests that need human judgement about the look
Tests of features that nobody uses
explanation: Stable, repetitive, high-value checks such as regression and smoke tests.

stem: What should a good bug report contain?
options: Steps to reproduce, expected and actual results, and environment
Only the word error and the date it happened in most cases at that stage
The name of the developer who wrote the code in the long run at that stage
A guess about which line is the cause
explanation: Steps to reproduce, expected and actual result, environment and evidence such as screenshots.

stem: What is regression testing?
options: Re-testing existing features after a change
Testing a new feature for the very first time
Testing the system with very many users
Testing the software by reading its source code
explanation: Re-testing existing features after a change to make sure nothing broke.

stem: A field accepts ages from 18 to 60. Which values are the boundary values to test?
explanation: Boundary value analysis tests values at and around the limits: 17, 18, 60, 61.

stem: What does equivalence partitioning do?
options: Groups inputs treated alike and tests one value per group
Splits the test team into equal groups
Divides the code into equally sized modules within the team
Runs each test case on two environments for the project in day-to-day work
explanation: It groups inputs that the system should treat the same way and tests one value per group.

stem: Time is short and the release cannot move. How should you prioritise the tests?
options: Test the highest-risk and most-used features first
Test the features in the order they were built in practice
Test just the features that are easy to automate first
Skip testing and rely on user feedback after release
explanation: Risk-based testing: test the highest-risk and most-used features first.
